mainTopic: Counted items that cannot be cancelled: the משנה in ערלה, the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש over רבי מאיר's wording, and how רבי יוחנן explains the ruling about a forbidden animal
overview: The גמרא quotes the end of a משנה about forbidden crops, such as ערלה and כלאי הכרם, that got mixed into permitted ones. רבי מאיר says that anything usually sold by count is too important to be cancelled out (בטל), so the whole mixture must be burned. The חכמים say only six special items are that important, and רבי עקיבא adds a seventh. Anything else is cancelled out in 201. The משנה then sorts the items: tree fruits forbid as ערלה, and vegetables forbid as כלאי הכרם. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue whether רבי מאיר's rule reads 'את שדרכו למנות' (only things always counted) or 'כל שדרכו למנות' (anything sometimes counted). The גמרא then repeats its earlier question: our משנה rules that a forbidden animal is not cancelled, which fits ריש לקיש but seems hard for רבי יוחנן. רב פפא answers that, for רבי יוחנן, this ruling follows the תנא of the ליטרא of dried figs, whose words are quoted on the next amud.

steps.title: Mixed bundles: רבי מאיר says burn all, the חכמים say cancelled in 201
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה finishes a case of forbidden bundles that must be burned. It then gives a dispute about what happens if they get mixed into other bundles.
steps.simpleTranslation: They must be burned. If they got mixed with others, and those others with yet others, all of them must be burned. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: they are cancelled out in 201.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a משנה. This line finishes a case of forbidden bundles and then asks what happens when they get mixed into other bundles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds the forbidden bundle never gets cancelled, so the whole mixture, and even a mixture of that mixture, must be burned. The חכמים hold the normal rule for ערלה and כלאי הכרם: one forbidden piece among 200 permitted pieces is cancelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: They must be burned
They became mixed together
They are cancelled out (literally 'they go up')
201: one forbidden item in 200 permitted ones

steps.confusionAlert: The first word, 'יִדָּלְקוּ', belongs to the end of a sentence that started before this section. It is not a new case.

phrases.english: They must be burned.
phrases.notes: This finishes the previous line of the משנה, about bundles of a forbidden crop.

phrases.english: If they became mixed with others,
(and those others with yet others),
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some leave them out.

phrases.english: all of them must be burned.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
They are cancelled out in two hundred and one.
phrases.notes: This means one forbidden bundle mixed with 200 permitted ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a משנה that the גמרא began quoting before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: the mixture is never cancelled and everything is burned. חכמים: the mixture is cancelled in 201.

steps.title: Why רבי מאיר forbids: items that are counted cannot be cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives רבי מאיר's reason: anything usually counted is too important to be cancelled. The חכמים limit this to six items, and רבי עקיבא adds a seventh.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי מאיר used to say: anything that is usually counted forbids its mixture. The חכמים say: only six items forbid their mixture. רבי עקיבא says seven. These are: nuts with brittle shells, pomegranates of באדן, sealed barrels, beet greens, cabbage stalks, and Greek gourd. רבי עקיבא adds: also a homeowner's loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the reason behind רבי מאיר's ruling and gives the חכמים's much shorter list of items that cannot be cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that something sold one by one, rather than by weight, is important, and an important item cannot be cancelled out. רבי מאיר applies this to anything that is counted. The חכמים apply it only to six named items, and רבי עקיבא adds home-baked loaves as a seventh.

keyTerms.meaning: Its usual way is to be counted (sold by number, not by weight)
Makes the mixture forbidden
Nuts with thin, brittle shells
Pomegranates from the place called באדן
Loaves baked by a homeowner

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that a counted item is important and cannot be cancelled, is the idea the next step will argue about.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Meir used to say:
Anything whose usual way is to be counted forbids its mixture.
phrases.notes: Here 'מְקַדֵּשׁ' does not mean 'makes holy'. It means the item makes the whole mixture forbidden.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ מְקַדֵּשׁ אֶלָּא שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: Only six items forbid their mixture.
Rabbi Akiva says: seven,
and these are they: nuts with brittle shells,
pomegranates of Badan, and sealed barrels,
beet greens, and cabbage stalks,
and Greek gourd.
Rabbi Akiva adds:
Also a homeowner's loaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבי מאיר's ruling in step 1 and the חכמים's narrower view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: every counted item cannot be cancelled. חכמים: only six specific items cannot be cancelled. רבי עקיבא: seven items, adding a homeowner's loaves.

steps.title: Which items forbid as ערלה and which as כלאי הכרם
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains that each listed item forbids its mixture under the prohibition that fits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whatever can be ערלה forbids its mixture as ערלה. Whatever can be כלאי הכרם forbids its mixture as כלאי הכרם.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה clarifies which prohibition applies to each item on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fruits of trees (nuts, pomegranates, and wine from grapes in the barrels) can be ערלה. Vegetables (beets, cabbage, and gourd) can be כלאי הכרם when planted in a vineyard. Each item forbids its mixture under its own prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit from a tree's first three years, which is forbidden
Other crops planted in a vineyard, which are forbidden
That which is fit for (can fall under)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list: important, counted items cannot be cancelled. Tree fruits forbid as ערלה, and vegetables forbid as כלאי הכרם.

phrases.english: Whatever can be orla forbids as orla,
phrases.notes: These are the nuts, the pomegranates and the wine barrels.

phrases.english: whatever can be diverse kinds of the vineyard forbids as diverse kinds of the vineyard.
phrases.notes: These are the beets, the cabbage and the gourd.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sorts the list from step 2 into the two prohibitions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each item forbids its mixture under the prohibition it can belong to: ערלה or כלאי הכרם.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue: 'את' or 'כל' in רבי מאיר's rule
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים argue about the exact wording of רבי מאיר's rule, and that wording changes how wide the rule is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was said about this: רבי יוחנן says we learned 'את שדרכו למנות'. רבי שמעון בן לקיש says we learned 'כל שדרכו למנות'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an argument between אמוראים over one word in רבי מאיר's rule. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, the wording is 'את', meaning only items that are always counted cannot be cancelled. According to ריש לקיש, the wording is 'כל', meaning anything that is even sometimes counted cannot be cancelled. So ריש לקיש's version makes רבי מאיר's rule much broader.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was said about it: introduces an argument between אמוראים on a source
That whose way is: only the thing that is always counted
Anything whose way is: even something only sometimes counted

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an argument about whether רבי מאיר is right. Both agree on what רבי מאיר said in general; they argue only about one word in his rule and how wide it reaches.
steps.whyThisMatters: How wide 'counted' reaches decides which items can be cancelled, and the גמרא will build on this argument.

phrases.english: And it was said about it:
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
We learned 'that whose way is to be counted,'
phrases.notes: He means only items that are always counted.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
We learned 'anything whose way is to be counted.'
phrases.notes: He means even items that are only sometimes counted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי מאיר's rule in step 2 and argues about its exact wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: 'את' (only things always counted). ריש לקיש: 'כל' (anything sometimes counted).

steps.title: The animal ruling fits ריש לקיש, but what about רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: The ruling that a forbidden animal is not cancelled fits ריש לקיש's wide wording of רבי מאיר's rule. It seems hard to explain with רבי יוחנן's narrow wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for ריש לקיש. But according to רבי יוחנן, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its earlier question about our משנה in זבחים, which rules that a forbidden animal mixed with others is not cancelled. That ruling works with ריש לקיש's version of רבי מאיר's rule, but not easily with רבי יוחנן's version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ריש לקיש's wide version, anything that is even sometimes counted is too important to be cancelled, so animals are included. In רבי יוחנן's narrow version, animals do not qualify, because they are not sold only by count. If so, a forbidden animal should be cancelled by a simple majority, and the ruling needs a new explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well / this is fine
But (introduces the side that has a problem)
What can be said? (a challenge asking for an explanation)

phrases.english: This works out well according to Reish Lakish,
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש's wording of רבי מאיר's rule is the wider one from Step 4, so animals count as important.

phrases.english: but according to Rabbi Yochanan
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the wording argument from Step 4 to repeat the earlier question about our משנה's ruling that a forbidden animal is not cancelled.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's narrow wording of רבי מאיר's rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the narrow wording, animals are not important enough to escape cancellation. Yet the ruling says a forbidden animal is not cancelled.

steps.title: רב פפא: this ruling follows the תנא of the ליטרא of dried figs
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that, according to רבי יוחנן, the animal ruling comes from a different תנא, the one in the case of a ליטרא of dried figs. The גמרא then starts quoting that תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: This תנא is the תנא of the ליטרא of dried figs, who says:
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question by saying the ruling about animals follows another תנא's view. The line ends with 'who says,' which sets up a quote that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not have to read the animal ruling through his narrow wording of רבי מאיר's rule. רב פפא links the ruling to the תנא of the dried-figs case, whose own principle can explain why the animal is not cancelled. The details of that principle come in the quote that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period whose opinion is being followed
A litra, a unit of weight
Dried figs
Who says (introduces a quote)

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not taking ריש לקיש's side. He is still answering for רבי יוחנן, by tracing the ruling to a different תנא.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא – תַּנָּא דְּלִיטְרָא קְצִיעוֹת הוּא,
phrases.english: This tanna is the tanna of the litra of dried figs,
phrases.notes: 'This tanna' means the one who rules that a forbidden animal is not cancelled.

phrases.english: who says:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַאי תַּנָּא – תַּנָּא דְּלִיטְרָא קְצִיעוֹת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 5 for רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Links the ruling to a different תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animal ruling seemed to depend on רבי מאיר's counted-items rule, which in רבי יוחנן's narrow wording does not include animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוחנן, the ruling follows the תנא of the ליטרא of dried figs. His view is quoted at the start of the next amud.
